pr_title: Fix viewport scaling at intermediate resolutions
pr_body:
Fixes #102656: viewport scale is wrong at resolutions that are not integer multiples of content_scale_factor.

This is done by allowing size_2d_override to be Size2 instead of Size2i. This change is ~propagated to keep the exposed SubViewport consistent with the underlying implementation~ _not propagated_ to SubViewport to keep compatibility for now.

**Note:**
I see the output of `Viewport::get_visible_rect()` get treated as a Rect2i in some places, even though it returns a Rect2. Before this change, this might have been accidentally correct, since it was generated from either `size` or `size_2d_override`, which were both Size2i. It might need a second look to make sure it still works correctly, because I'm not exactly sure what all these code fragments do.
pr_comments:
Pushed a change that does not expose this to SubViewport to avoid the compatibility warnings. (As a side note, these do not pop up in my local tests for some reason, how would I fix this?)

If someone could point me towards some resources on what kind of compatibility are we talking about here, and what is the usual philosophy that the dev team follows, that would be super appreciated. (Is it compatibility for users between versions? Is it API/ABI compatibility?)

The compatibility notes doesn't occur locally because it's a dedicated check, but this breaks compatibility because the type changes, and that can't be done trivially

You would probably need to register compatibility methods, see [here](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/contributing/development/handling_compatibility_breakages.html) for instructions 

If this can be done in a way that doesn't break compatibility it should, if unavoidable it can be evaluated
One last try, forgot to revert the property registration itself to Vector2i.
The methods will still be registered with the changed type I think, so that will still break compatibility unless the bound methods also don't use `Vector2`
Bound methods should all be Vector2i, only the internals are working with Vector2.
I think this one is only waiting for a last review from the core team and a merge now :)
We're in release freeze for 4.4 and only merging regression fixes now, so this will first be merged for 4.5 after 4.4-stable is released. It's already queued for merge in 4.5-dev1.

issue_context.title: Window content_scale_factor causes jitter in Control size
issue_context.body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in 4.4-beta3, 4.3-stable

### System information

Godot v4.4.beta3 - Ubuntu 24.04.1 LTS 24.04 on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - integrated Intel(R) UHD Graphics (CML GT2) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-10510U CPU @ 1.80GHz (8 threads)

### Issue description

Using the recommended way to scale UI to screen resolution by setting `get_tree().root.content_scale_factor` (either in the project settings or from script) causes Control node pixels to jitter on resizing the window. This is true even when the "Snap Controls to Pixels" option is enabled.

Interestingly, using the node's own scale factor (or scaling a parent node to rescale the entire UI) doesn't exhibit this behaviour, but causes a host of other issues with GUIs so it's not a possible workaround.

Screenshot of misaligned grid pixels from the MRP:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c906e43d-2bce-4ecd-b48a-aae6f9bb0015)

Screenshot of the grid looking perfect at a different resolution:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fb2dea18-5215-41d1-b84b-93b6cceea017)

I also managed to reproduce this in my game with all kinds of control nodes, including fonts. In that case the jitter is a lot more visible even when resizing at high resolutions.

**Update:**

Setting `content_scale_factor = 8.0` shows that this is not even a jitter, the control node's scale is just completely off when resizing to certain resolutions. There's no need for Nearest filtering either, the effect is clearly visible even on Linear filtered textures.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3cf1038a-1958-488d-acf5-fd5148140f8e

### Steps to reproduce

1. Place a control node (Confirmed with: TextureRect, Label).
3. Optionally, set the window resolution to a small value, such as 480x360. For me small window sizes (regardless of the base resolution) greatly exacerbate the effect, but it also happens from time to time on larger window sizes.
4. Set `display/window/stretch/scale` to a larger value, in my case 4.0 is enough, 8.0 makes it super visible.
5. Resize the game window by dragging the corner, and watch the control node size jitter.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[gui-scale.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18734113/gui-scale.zip)
comments:
- Related to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/101562 and https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/83679.

I'm guessing Snap Controls to Pixels is always relative to the base viewport size, not the current window size (and current viewport resolution).

However, I'm not sure this is what you are noticing here. Snap Controls to Pixels does **not** perform integer scaling, so if you are resizing the window, you will be getting fractional scale factors (which makes nearest-neighbor-filtered textures look bad). You need to set the stretch scale policy to `integer` in the Project Settings for that to happen instead.

Setting the stretch policy to integer doesn't solve the problem, it doesn't have any effect with stretch mode "disabled".

If you check in the MRP, the control is _not actually being resized_. It stays the same size no matter the size of the window, it just seems to pick up some kind of noise. I'm suspecting it might be a floating point precision problem in some transforms, from multiplying then dividing with the scale value.

Using a larger `content_scale_factor` really shows what's happening, it's not even a pixel jitter or a fp precision thing. Controls are just straight up scaled wrong based on the window size. 

This is with `content_scale_factor = 8.0`:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3cf1038a-1958-488d-acf5-fd5148140f8e

Again, stretch mode is set to "disabled", there should be _nothing_ happening to control nodes when resizing the window.

Also, the wiggle is the exact same even with texture filtering set to linear, it's just less noticeable on small filtered textures. 

Turning off Snap Controls to Pixels also seems to have no effect, so I'm not sure about the relation to #83679
I wonder if this is what causes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/86563.

Could very well be!

I found out that this is not limited to controls after all, I was just correcting everything else with a camera transform in my original project. Without that, everything in the window is rendered with the wrong scale at certain resolutions.

I dug around a little bit and I think the cause is that content scale is implemented using the size override in the Viewport/Window class. But size override is clamped to integers, so only resolutions that divide by content_scale_factor result in a correct scaling.

I'll try and patch it out tonight, see if it breaks anything if I allow the override value to be a float.

@Calinou  I've checked, the fix for this doesn't directly fix #86563, but the problem could have been partially caused by this.

There are some more integer values in the calculations for the different aspect ratios and stretch modes, but they are a bit more complex and harder to follow than the one for stretch mode "disabled" :) Maybe someone who has more experience with the aspect and viewport calculations could take a second look at it.

No, the reason it needs to be a float is because the original assumption that `size_2d_override` (aka the size of the viewport in render-space) can be described as a Vector2i just doesn't hold in general. A side effect of this assumption is the bug that we are fixing in the first place.

Changing only that one part where this bug manifests leaves the class in an inconsistent state, where certain assumptions that you would expect won't hold anymore.

For example, `stretch_transform.scale != size / size_2d_override` which would be a very reasonable thing to expect, and other code might depend on in.
